meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have about twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.

"The checker said 94%." That's a machine's guess, and your own school's procedure, section 4.3, says software results do not by themselves establish a concern. So what else do you have, and did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal

Hale,

Nothing was agreed at today's meeting. I still require that the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: "The checker said 94%", because it gave her a software score as the only basis, which her printed procedure says isn't enough on its own.
Try next time: in your first line, own that the zero went in before anyone called home, then show her a dated document from Owen's own work instead of the score.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
